text:
mike: seeing a sudden p99 spike from sjc pop starting ~08:10 UTC, correlates with a drop in throughput. digging now.

jessica: yup saw alerts — p50 ~25ms -> 60ms, p99 -> 1.8s. requests/sec down ~30%. any known deploy?

alan: no deploys in sjc at that time. netops flagged a BGP weight change from provider-side around 08:09. might be steering traffic off the usual egress.

mike: digging runtime traces — lots of "kernel fallback" events on small batches. looks like kernel selector suddenly preferred fallback path for many hosts. attaching snippet from trace:

mike: ```
[08:11:02] host=svc-rt-12 kernel=quant-fallback reason=splice_miss seq_len=64 batch_sz=1 cpu_ms=2.8
[08:11:02] host=svc-rt-12 kvcache.eviction=1 kvcache.miss=17 kv_lookup_ms=4.2
[08:11:03] host=svc-rt-13 kernel=fast-attn chosen=false candidate_score_delta=-1.7
```

liam: interesting — if peering weight shift pushed more traffic to a set of noisy hosts we might see smaller concurrent batches and colder KV caches, causing both kernel mis-selection and kv thrash.

jessica: netops, can you confirm what changed on the peering side? @netops

netops: confirmed — upstream asked to rebalance weights to a different colo for congestion. it changed our egress distribution for ~4m starting 08:09. we rolled it back at 08:14 due to visible impact.

alan: rollback matches partial recovery window in metrics. but we still see degraded kernel selection for ~12m after rollback. suspect KV cache starvation and sampler heuristics reacting to the transient.

mike: ran perf-profile on an affected host, result: scheduler runnable_avg jumped, syscalls per request increased (epoll thrash). pasted flame snippet (trimmed):

mike: ```
scheduler 35% | kernel-selector 18% | kv-cache-lookup 14% | net-io 12% | decode 9% | others 12%
kv-cache: cold-start tasks show increased lock contention on shard 3
```

jessica: we have a recent heuristic change that reduces batch wait timeout when predicted latency >150ms to avoid tail amplification. could that have amplified small-batch behavior?

alan: yes — heuristics saw rising lat and shortened window -> batches smaller -> kernel selector scores based on batch size tilted toward fallback kernels, which are slower per-token for our model shape. feedback loop.

liam: hypothesis: network steering -> uneven host load -> small batches + cold KV -> kernel fallback + kv evictions -> higher latency -> heuristic shortens windows -> smaller batches -> repeat.

oncall: mitigation suggestion: 1) temporarily pin kernel selector to prefer fast-attn for model-x on sjc hosts 2) increase kv-cache ttl for that pop 3) pause the batch-timeout heuristic for 15m. I'll run changes if owners ack.

jessica: ack to all three. we should do them in that order: pin kernel, bump kv ttl, then pause heuristic. do we have a safe rollback plan?

mike: safe rollback: remove kernel pin + revert ttl + re-enable heuristic. changes are per-pop flags via runtime-config so rollback is quick.

netops: we will keep peering rollback in place and monitor. if provider retries weight shift we'll coordinate.

liam: also toggled a lighter KV warmup on ingress path to prefetch recent prefixes for the bursty cohort — it's running as a canary on 2 hosts.

mike: applied kernel pin on 4/6 hosts at 08:25. immediate effect: p99 down from 1.8s -> 420ms, throughput recovered ~20%.

jessica: bumped kv-cache TTL from 60s -> 300s at 08:28 for sjc. after that kv miss rate dropped ~70% on affected hosts.

mike: paused batch-timeout heuristic at 08:30. a/b test shows batch sizes returned to ~6 avg (was 2-3). end-to-end latency p50~22ms p99~180ms at 08:35.

oncall: good. documentable next steps: - add guard to batch-timeout heuristic so it doesn't flip when many hosts change routing simultaneously - add kernel-selector hysteresis to avoid switching on transient small-batch signals - add an egress-peering watcher to correlate weight changes with host batch patterns

alan: also want a post-incident perf regression test: replay recent traffic shape against kernel selector logic to check for mis-selection windows. I'll file the eval.

liam: opened ticket #INF-8432 with traces, perf profiles, and the kvcache eviction histograms. owner: alan.

jessica: final ask: product wants a short blurb about customer impact. summary: brief latency spike for ~20m in SJC due to upstream peering weight change that caused host-level small-batch and KV cache starvation; mitigations applied (kernel pin, kvcache ttl, heuristic pause) restored normal performance.

mike: +1. will attach charts and timeline to INF-8432. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
